turns.question: What follow-up steps does the heart failure discharge protocol require after a patient goes home, and by when?

report.markdown:
Based on the Riverside Health Network Heart Failure Discharge and Transitional Care Protocol (RHN-CLN-HF-014 v4.2), the protocol requires the following post-discharge follow-up steps for patients discharged to **home or home health** [1]:

| Follow-up Step | Required Action | Timing | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **48-hour nurse call** | Phone call covering symptoms, daily weight, medicines in hand, open checklist items | Within 48 hours of discharge (up to 3 attempts documented) | Care Transitions RN |
| **7-day follow-up visit** | In-person or telehealth visit at an HF clinic (Pine Valley Heart Failure Clinic F10, Oakridge Cardiology Clinic F11), primary care clinic | Within 7 calendar days of discharge (visit must be kept; a phone call does not count) | Receiving clinic |
| **14-day labs** | Basic metabolic panel (potassium, creatinine) after any change to diuretic, ARNI, ACE inhibitor, or MRA dose | Within 14 days of discharge; result reviewed within 2 business days | Ordering clinic |
| **30-day clinic review** | Cardiology/HF clinic review of volume status and titration of guideline-directed therapy; repeat education items if readmitted | Within 30 days of discharge | Cardiology |
| **90-day assessment** | Functional status, medication adherence, need for repeat echocardiogram | At 90 days (closes the transitional care episode) | Primary care or HF clinic |

**If the 7-day visit is missed:** The Care Transitions nurse calls the patient the same day (end of day 7), reschedules within 2 business days, records the reason, escalates to the Care Transitions manager if still not completed by day 10, and includes the patient in the monthly missed follow-up report [1].

**Note:** Patients discharged to a skilled nursing facility, inpatient rehabilitation, or against medical advice follow a different schedule (Section 6) and are not counted in the 7-day completion measure. Discharges to hospice are excluded from all measures.

5. Post-discharge follow-up schedule
5.1 The 7-day visit
The visit must take place within 7 calendar days of the discharge date. The clinic confirms the appointment by phone 2 days before it. Transport is arranged by Care Transitions for any patient who has no ride. A visit on day 7 counts; a visit on day 8 or later is recorded as late and still prompts the 14-day actions.

Heart Failure Discharge and Transitional Care
Protocol
1. Purpose and scope
2. Definitions
Index discharge. The discharge that ends an inpatient HF admission. Discharges that end in death or in transfer to hospice are not index discharges for quality reporting.
Eligible for the 7-day visit. An index discharge to home or to home health. Patients discharged to a skilled nursing facility, to inpatient rehabilitation or against medical advice follow section 6.
Completed follow-up visit. A kept outpatient encounter, in person or by telehealth, with a physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant at a Riverside clinic or hospital outpatient department. A phone call from the Care Transitions nurse does not count as a visit.
30-day readmission. Any later inpatient admission of the same patient that begins within 30 days of the index discharge, whatever its cause.

5.2 Missed or unbooked visits
If the 7-day visit has not been completed by the end of day 7, the Care Transitions nurse:
- calls the patient the same day and reschedules the visit within 2 business days;
- records the reason (no transport, patient declined, clinic capacity, other);
- escalates to the Care Transitions manager if the visit is still not completed by day 10; and
- lists the patient in the monthly missed follow-up report that goes to the Clinical Quality Committee.
Home or home health, What this protocol requires = Full schedule in section 5; counted in the 7-day completion measure. Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehabilitation, What this protocol requires = Discharge summary and medication list to the facility within 24 hours; facility physician reviews within 72 hours of arrival; not counted in the 7-day measure. Against medical advice, What this protocol requires = Care Transitions calls within 24 hours and offers a visit within 7 days; not counted in the 7-day measure. Hospice, What this protocol requires = Palliative plan of care; excluded from every measure in section 8

3. Discharge readiness criteria
The discharging physician confirms and documents each criterion before the discharge order is signed. The Care Transitions nurse completes the discharge checklist (form RHN-F-0231) in parallel; a scanned copy is filed in the chart.
- • Weight is at or within 3 lb of the documented dry weight, and the discharge weight is recorded on the checklist.
- • Oral diuretic regimen has been stable for at least 24 hours with no intravenous diuretic in that period.
- • Potassium and creatinine from the last 24 hours have been reviewed.
- • Resting heart rate and blood pressure are within the targets the cardiology team has written in the plan of care.

hits.snippet:
Heart Failure Discharge and Transitional Care
Protocol
1. Purpose and scope
This protocol sets out how Riverside Health Network prepares adult patients with heart failure (HF) for discharge and how it supports them in the 90 days afterwards. Its goal is to cut avoidable 30-day readmissions by making the first week after discharge predictable: every eligible patient leaves with a scheduled follow-up visit, a working home scale, a reconciled medication list and a named nurse who will call within 48 hours.
The protocol applies to every inpatient admission whose primary diagnosis is heart failure (ICD-10 codes I50.x, for example I50.9 heart failure unspecified, I50.22 chronic systolic heart failure, I50.23 acute on chronic systolic heart failure and I50.32 chronic diastolic heart failure) at Riverside Memorial Hospital (F01), Lakeview Community Hospital (F02) and Eastgate Regional Hospital (F03). Patients with HF as a secondary diagnosis follow the unit’s general discharge process, with this protocol's education items as a recommended addition.

Heart Failure Discharge and Transitional Care

6. Other discharge destinations
A patient readmitted within 30 days of an HF discharge is reviewed by the unit’s nurse manager and the Care Transitions manager within 5 business days. The review asks which schedule steps were missed and whether the patient could have been supported differently.
Discharging physician, Responsibility = Confirms the readiness criteria in section 3 and writes the plan of care. Unit nurse, Responsibility = Completes the checklist, performs teach-back, confirms the home scale, books the 7-day visit. Pharmacist, Responsibility = Reconciles medicines and reviews the discharge list. Care Transitions RN, Responsibility = Makes the 48-hour call, owns the schedule, rescheduled missed visits, reports open items. Receiving clinic, Responsibility = Holds capacity for HF visits within 7 days and reports no-shows the same day. Care Transitions manager, Responsibility = Reviews escalations and readmissions; reports monthly to the Clinical Quality Committee
